# How to contribute to Siftyan

Software licensing is a complex and nuanced field. If you have an interest in open source software, software licensing, or just want to help build a useful tool for the community you're welcome to contribute! See [README.md](../README.md#installation) for information on how to set up your development environment. Here are some ways you can contribute:

## Follow the Code of Conduct 📜
We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive environment for all contributors. Please read and always follow our Code of Conduct, which can be found in the [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) file in our repository.

## Report Issues 🪲
**If you find a security vulnerability, DO NOT OPEN an issue. Please report it privately by emailing us at siftyan@outlook.com.**

If you find a bug, have a feature request, or want to suggest an improvement, please open an issue on our GitHub repository. Before creating an issue, make sure to search for [existing issues](https://github.com/AbdulMuizz789/siftyan/issues) to avoid duplicates. Be sure to provide as much detail as possible, including steps to reproduce the issue if applicable and any relevant screenshots or error messages. Use the provided [issue templates](ISSUE_TEMPLATE) to help us understand and address your issue more effectively.

## Submit Code Contributions 💻 
If you want to contribute code that changes more than one or two lines, please fork the repository and create a **new branch** for your changes. Once you've made your changes, submit a pull request with a *clear description* of what you've done and why. We will review your pull request and provide feedback. Testing your changes locally before submitting a pull request is highly recommended.

We would also appreciate if you could write meaningful commit messages and follow the existing code style and conventions.

### Example of a good commit message:
```
git commit -m "Fix license normalization for pip dependencies"
```

## Feature and Enhancement Contributions 🚀
The goal of Siftyan is to provide a comprehensive and accurate license compliance report for projects. It is a lightweight local-first tool meant for developers who need to ensure their projects comply with various licenses.

If you have an idea for a new feature or an enhancement to an existing feature, please open an issue to discuss it before starting work. This allows us to provide feedback and ensure that the feature aligns with the project's goals. Once the feature is approved, you can proceed with implementing it and submitting a pull request as described above.

## Documentation Contributions 📚
If you want to contribute to the documentation, please fork the repository and create a **new branch** for your changes. Once you've made your changes, submit a pull request with a *clear description* of what you've done and why. We will review your pull request and provide feedback.

## Join the Discussion 💬
We welcome discussions about the project, whether it's about design decisions, feature ideas, or general feedback. You can join the discussion on our GitHub repository or reach out to us on social media.

# Code Review Process
The core contributors will review pull requests regularly to ensure that they meet the project's standards and guidelines. We encourage constructive feedback and collaboration during the review process. Please be patient, as it may take some time for your pull request to be reviewed. Expect to hear from us within 1-2 weeks. If you haven't received feedback within that time frame, feel free to politely follow up on your pull request.
